solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Work space vacated round Post Office counter

indicators.note: the work and the emptied space are placed around the Post Office abbreviation

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, so only the outside letters of the word space remain

explanation.surface: Someone empties a workspace around the counter of a post office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a shop or post office counter, but it is a verb meaning resist.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter an argument is to resist or argue against it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: At sea, repose around dock, or put into dock

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around a word for dock
being at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to dock is to cut

explanation.surface: A sailor resting at sea, around a dock, or being tried in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The two docks differ: the first means cut short, the second is the defendant's box in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a defendant into the court's dock is to bring a criminal case against them.

clue.text: Game of cards one's left on the shelf

definitions.meaning: a simple children's card game of pairing
an unmarried woman thought past marrying age

explanation.surface: A card game that leaves one player stranded on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a children's card game and a dated term for a spinster.

clue.text: Girl welcome to come round

indicators.note: coming round means turning about, so the word is reversed

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting or welcome

explanation.surface: A girl is welcome to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name.

clue.text: National emblem a rhinestone?

definitions.meaning: the three-leafed clover symbol of Ireland
a rhinestone is imitation jewellery, a fake gem: read as two words

explanation.surface: Asking whether a glittering paste gem could serve as a country's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second reading: SHAM (fake) ROCK (gem).
explanation.definitionFit: The clover-like plant is the emblem of Ireland, worn on St Patrick's Day.

clue.text: In recital, did rock and roll material

indicators.note: a recital is spoken aloud, so what follows is taken by its sound

parts.note: swayed means moved to and fro, rocked and rolled

explanation.surface: At a performance, a musician played rock and roll in some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock and roll' looks like the music genre but is just motion; think of Blue Suede Shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather with a napped finish is a fabric or material.

clue.text: Drink a day before agitation

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
till means until, before
ado means fuss, agitation

explanation.surface: Having a drink the day before getting worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-dry sherry from Spain, a type of drink.

clue.text: Country that's had burning desire to depose leading couple

indicators.note: deposing removes the rulers at the head, here the opening two letters

parts.note: pyromania is a compulsive urge to set fires

explanation.surface: A country with a burning urge to overthrow its ruling couple.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to the Ceausescus, the Romanian ruling couple deposed in 1989.
explanation.definitionFit: A country in south-east Europe, on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Penned record covering a number of years

indicators.note: one word covers the other, wrapping around it

parts.note: CD, compact disc, is a record
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: Writing a record covering several years.
explanation.definitionFit: Penned here means shut in a pen, enclosed, as an animal in a cage.

clue.text: Daring fellow, great and emphatic type

parts.note: daring means bold
ace means excellent, great

explanation.surface: Describing a bold man and his great, emphatic personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy-stroked printing letters used for emphasis are called by this name in typography.

clue.text: I'm surprised by one like Gandalf's resistance

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
Gandalf, the wizard of Tolkien's books, is a mage

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise from someone resisted by a wizard like Gandalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance measured in ohms is called by this technical term.

clue.text: Evidently embarrassed over complaint for going off track

indicators.note: in a down-or-across sense, over tells us to turn the word for blushing backwards

parts.note: someone visibly embarrassed is red in the face
an ailment is an illness, a complaint

explanation.surface: Someone visibly embarrassed about a grievance concerning a train leaving the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A train leaving its rails is the noun sense of an accident on the railway.

clue.text: Girl with bad back, a shade yellow

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name

indicators.note: placed after the word for bad, back tells us to write it in reverse

parts.note: evil means bad
red is a shade, a colour

explanation.surface: A girl with a bad back has gone a shade of yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and this compound adjective means cowardly too.

clue.text: Prompt to dispose of grand artwork

indicators.note: getting rid of something means removing a letter from the prompting word

parts.note: to prompt someone is to nudge them
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A prompt urging someone to sell off a grand work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or sculpture of an unclothed figure is itself called by this name in art.

clue.text: Play day in pool

parts.note: play means fun, amusement

explanation.surface: A day of playing in a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool of money is a shared stock of cash, a synonym.

clue.text: Desperate sellers do a sales booster

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Struggling vendors try anything to push up their sales.
explanation.definitionFit: A product sold below cost to attract customers who then buy other goods boosts sales.

clue.text: Part of issue paper's spoken of

indicators.note: being spoken of means said aloud, so the sound counts

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; 's is is

explanation.surface: Part of an edition of a paper that is talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid. 'issue' means offspring, not an edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, and a male child is one of them.

clue.text: Pick extremely raunchy clothing providing thrill

parts.note: to elect is to pick

indicators.note: the outer letters dress the word for providing, around it
the extremes of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: if means providing that

explanation.surface: Choosing very racy clothing gives someone a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like garments in the surface but signals one piece wrapping another.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite or give a jolt, figuratively a charge of electricity.

clue.text: Island with crude oil and panache

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An island blessed with crude oil and a certain style.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek island in the Ionian Sea, the largest of that group.

clue.text: In kitchen, peckish shrews may do so

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Hungry little animals nibble away in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrews' suggests the small mammals, but means nagging wives.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewish wives nag their husbands, the sense of this verb.

clue.text: Song's main performer in audition

definitions.note: 's stands for is: the definition is a song

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: the lead is the principal performer

explanation.surface: Choosing a song's main singer at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: The German word for song is said 'leed', like the noun for a star role.
explanation.definitionFit: A German art song, as composed by Schubert, is known by this name.

clue.text: One listing housing right for student?

indicators.note: housing means holding inside

parts.note: something listing tilts over, so it is a leaner

explanation.surface: A person compiling lists of accommodation for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone studying a subject or skill, such as a driver with L-plates, is a pupil.

clue.text: Make miserable baguette?

definitions.meaning: to cause distress or hurt someone
the French for bread, a baguette being a French loaf

explanation.surface: A baguette that would make anyone miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the second sense is French.
explanation.definitionFit: To distress someone is to hurt them; in French the same spelling means bread.

clue.text: A couple of leaves? Or as many as you like

indicators.note: a couple means two of them, so the word is doubled

parts.note: goes means leaves, with go as the verb leave

explanation.surface: Asking if a plant has two leaves or plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: This French-derived phrase means in abundance, plenty.

clue.text: Vile scenes broadcast on TV, ideas close to savagery

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A complaint about nasty TV content inspiring savage ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid term for horror films on videocassette deemed obscene, full of vile scenes.

clue.text: Figure it's what computer fans do?

parts.note: fans dig what they like, slang for enjoy
IT, information technology, stands for computing

explanation.surface: Wondering if this is what computer enthusiasts do.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'IT's what fans DIG': the two pieces swap order.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral from nought to nine is a figure.

clue.text: Make a fold in the same clothes

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same
gear means clothes

explanation.surface: Instructions to fold the same clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down a page corner is to crease it like a dog's ear, a verb.

clue.text: Very great job that's temporary and bizarre

parts.note: a gig is a one-off or short-term job
antic means grotesque, bizarre

explanation.surface: A temporary job turned out to be a huge and very strange one.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge or enormous in size, a synonym.

clue.text: Stick with unhappy, losing side from Liverpool

indicators.note: losing means a letter is lost

parts.note: glum means unhappy

indicators.note: the side of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: Remaining with a gloomy, defeated football team from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue or adhesive, the noun stuff that sticks.

clue.text: Spot president once at entertaining gathering

parts.note: James Polk was the eleventh US president

indicators.note: one word holds another as a host entertains a guest

parts.note: a do is a party, a gathering

explanation.surface: Spotting a former president at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: James Polk was US president in the 1840s.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern of regularly spaced spots, so one such spot, by extension.

clue.text: Maybe Thomas More's pretentious title captivates

definitions.note: 's stands for is; Thomas More is an example of the definition

indicators.note: holds captive, so the title goes around the other word

parts.note: Mr is a title
arty means pretentiously artistic

explanation.surface: Thomas More's grand title captivates people.
explanation.definitionFit: Executed for refusing to accept Henry VIII as church head, More is a Catholic saint who died for faith.
